mechanics.summary: A skill action uses two base dice: one for the selected skill level and one for that skill's connected attribute.
trigger: character performs an action using a skill
character has a level in that skill

unknowns: The selected skill is player or Referee input.

mechanics.summary: When the character has no level in the skill being used, roll only the connected attribute die.
trigger: character performs an action using a skill
character has no level in that skill

unknowns: The selected skill is player or Referee input.

mechanics.summary: A base die result of 6 or higher is one success; an action succeeds when at least one base die is a success.
trigger: base dice are rolled
exceptions: A D10 or D12 result of 10 or higher counts as two successes.

mechanics.summary: A single D10 or D12 base die result of 10 or higher contributes two successes.
trigger: D10 or D12 base die result is 10 or higher
exceptions: This outcome is not possible on a D6 or D8.

mechanics.summary: Successes beyond the first produce additional effects only where the rules explicitly state an additional effect.
trigger: roll has more than one success

outcome.value: apply only explicitly stated extra-success effects

unknowns: The applicable action rule must supply its own extra-success effect.

mechanics.summary: After an initial skill roll fails or has fewer desired successes, the actor can push by rerolling every die that shows neither a success nor a bane; retained dice are not rerolled and the prior result cannot be restored.
trigger: initial skill roll failed or actor wants additional successes
actor pushes roll

value.reroll: all dice without success or bane

exceptions: Passive or unaware rolls cannot be pushed.
A roll can be pushed only once.
Eligible ammo dice are also rerolled under the ammunition-dice procedure.

unknowns: Whether the actor wants to push and whether the initial action was active require input.

mechanics.summary: On a pushed STR- or AGL-based roll, each bane on a base die immediately deals 1 damage; on a pushed INT- or EMP-based roll, each such bane immediately causes 1 stress.
trigger: skill roll is pushed
base die shows bane
exceptions: If this damage incapacitates the actor, incapacitation occurs after the action resolves.
For a STR- or AGL-based roll using a tool, weapon, or vehicle, pushing damage affects the item instead.

unknowns: The count of bane results and whether an item was used must be available from roll and action context.

mechanics.summary: For a STR- or AGL-based skill roll using a tool, weapon, or vehicle, pushing damage affects that item instead of the actor and lowers its reliability rating.
trigger: STR- or AGL-based skill roll is pushed
tool, weapon, or vehicle used for the roll
base die shows bane

unknowns: Which item was used for the roll requires input.

mechanics.summary: When a roll is pushed, reroll its ammo dice that show neither a success nor a bane; each bane rolled on an ammo die damages the firearm and decreases its reliability rating.
trigger: roll with ammo dice is pushed

value.reroll: ammo dice without success or bane
value.baneEffect: decrease firearm reliability by one per bane

unknowns: Ammo-die count and results come from the weapon procedure.

mechanics.summary: Only a skill roll for an actively performed action can be pushed; a passive or unaware roll cannot be pushed.
trigger: actor attempts to push a skill roll
inputs: whether the actor actively performed the action
whether the actor was passive or unaware

outcome.value: block push for passive or unaware roll

unknowns: Active, passive, and unaware status are contextual determinations.

mechanics.summary: A skill roll can be pushed once only.
trigger: actor attempts to push an already pushed skill roll

mechanics.summary: For a shared challenge, the PCs choose one suitable actor to roll; other PCs can help when relevant.
trigger: PCs face a challenge together
exceptions: This rule does not apply in combat, where each PC acts independently.

unknowns: Group membership and choice of actor require input.

mechanics.summary: A failed group roll is a failure for the whole group; group members cannot make sequential individual attempts at the same challenge.
trigger: group roll fails

outcome.value: block one attempt per group member

exceptions: This rule does not apply in combat, where each PC acts independently.

unknowns: The challenged task's identity and retry scope require Referee input.

mechanics.summary: Each positive modifier step upgrades a base die by one die size and each negative modifier step downgrades a base die by one die size.
trigger: a skill-roll modifier applies
exceptions: Die balancing and minimum/maximum procedures apply.

mechanics.summary: Several modifiers can apply to the same skill roll and are cumulative.
trigger: multiple skill-roll modifiers apply

outcome.value: sum modifier values before stepping dice

unknowns: Whether contextual modifiers apply is supplied by the relevant printed rule or Referee.

mechanics.summary: Step up the lower base die first and downstep the higher base die first; dice cannot exceed two D12s, and downstepping beyond two D6s removes one die but cannot reduce the roll below one D6.
trigger: net modifier steps are applied to base dice
exceptions: A one-die roll without a skill uses its own first-upgrade procedure.

mechanics.summary: For a roll with no skill level and one base die, the first step up adds a D6; further step-ups improve that die as normal.
trigger: one-base-die roll receives positive modifier

mechanics.summary: Each eligible helper declared before the roll gives +1, to a maximum help modifier of +3.
trigger: other PC or NPC helps a skill roll
exceptions: Helpers must be physically present and able to support the action; the Referee has final say.
In combat, helping uses an action of the same speed as the supported action.

unknowns: Eligibility and declaration-before-roll require input or roll history.

mechanics.summary: To win an opposed roll, the active party must have more successes than the adversary; every adversary success eliminates one active-party success.
trigger: an opposed roll is resolved
exceptions: The parties can roll the same skill or different skills.

unknowns: Which party is active and which skills apply require input.

mechanics.summary: Only the active party can push an opposed roll, and it can choose to push after the opponent has rolled.
trigger: opposed roll has been rolled
active party considers pushing

outcome.value: active party may push after opponent roll

referenceData.notes: Maps printed attribute and skill levels to base-die types.
The printed core-skill list connects each listed skill to one attribute.
Exact duration varies by situation; the Referee tracks passage of time and determines when a unit passes.
